super_nodes.label: Foundation ML interatomic potentials and methods
super_nodes.gloss: A mix of universal machine-learned interatomic potentials (MACE, SevenNet, PET, UMA) with general regression tools (XGBoost, SISSO) and a few sequence models.

super_nodes.label: Graph neural network architectures
super_nodes.gloss: Cited works here are almost all graph neural network and equivariant architectures (GNNs, Equiformer, SE(3)-Transformers, Tensor Field Networks) for molecular and material modeling.

super_nodes.label: General ML tools and methods
super_nodes.gloss: A broad mix of general machine-learning methods and software (regression, clustering, optimizers, NumPy, pymatgen) plus a couple of unrelated specific studies; no single tight topic.

super_nodes.label: Materials databases and phase transitions
super_nodes.gloss: Centers on open materials databases (Materials Project, Open Catalyst, ColabFit) and their claims, alongside phase-field and melting-related methods (Cahn-Hilliard, Lindemann criterion).

super_nodes.label: Materials ML software and benchmarks
super_nodes.gloss: A mix of materials-informatics software, benchmarks, and databases (Matbench, Matminer, GNoME, MatPES) alongside emerging LLM-agent tools (MatPilot, LLMatDesign) for materials design.

super_nodes.label: Diverse machine-learned potential techniques
super_nodes.gloss: A diverse set of MLIP-related techniques and formulas: elastic averaging (Voigt-Reuss-Hill), force-field methods, activation functions, and superconductivity formulas (McMillan, Allen-Dynes); no single tight topic.

super_nodes.label: DFT variants and magnetic skyrmion prediction
super_nodes.gloss: Mostly DFT and its variants (DFT+U, vdW-DF, constrained DFT), including magnetic skyrmion prediction and ML models matching DFT-level formation-energy and band-structure accuracy.

super_nodes.label: Classical and ML interatomic potentials
super_nodes.gloss: Members are classical interatomic potentials (Finnis-Sinclair, MEAM, bond-order) and early machine-learned potentials (Behler-Parrinello, Deep Potential, NequIP, ACE) used for molecular dynamics simulation.

super_nodes.label: Phonon prediction with ML models
super_nodes.gloss: Nearly all members concern predicting phonon spectra and dispersion with ML/GNN models (Phonax, VGNN, PET-OAM) benchmarked against DFPT reference data.

super_nodes.label: Monte Carlo sampling and uncertainty
super_nodes.gloss: Centers on Monte Carlo sampling techniques (Metropolis, kinetic MC, umbrella sampling) plus uncertainty quantification and screening methods for ML-driven materials simulations.

super_nodes.label: Author citations and DFT corrections
super_nodes.gloss: Mostly author-name citations (Qi et al., Batzner et al.) plus a few DFT correction methods (Ewald, Harris-Foulkes, Blochl); no unifying topic besides being references.

super_nodes.label: Atomic descriptors and basis representations
super_nodes.gloss: Centers on descriptor and basis representations for atomic environments (Coulomb matrix, Gaussian and spherical-harmonic radial bases) and Gaussian-quadrature integration issues in potential-energy models.

super_nodes.label: Universal machine-learned interatomic potentials
super_nodes.gloss: Mostly universal or foundation machine-learned interatomic potentials (MACE, CHGNet, M3GNet, MatterSim, UMA, DPA, PET family), plus a few unrelated ML methods (ConvLSTM, XGBoost, SISSO).

super_nodes.label: Neural-network potential architectures
super_nodes.gloss: Almost entirely named neural-network architectures (GemNet, DimeNet, MEGNet, Orb, SevenNet, PhysNet, AIMNet2) for molecular and materials property or potential prediction.

super_nodes.label: Message-passing neural network architectures
super_nodes.gloss: Centers on message-passing and tensor-field neural network architectures (MPNN, TensorNet, Tensor Field Networks, Steerable CNNs) plus the deep-learning frameworks TensorFlow, PyTorch, and Keras.

super_nodes.label: Flow-matching generative models for crystal structures
super_nodes.gloss: Centers on flow-matching and normalizing-flow methods (F3flow, Force-Guided Bridge Matching, conditional normalizing flow) for generating or interpolating atomic structures, with pymatgen tooling support.

super_nodes.label: SE(3)/E(3)-equivariant neural network architectures
super_nodes.gloss: Almost entirely SE(3) and E(3)-equivariant neural network architectures (Equiformer, EquiformerV2, Clebsch-Gordan Nets, EQGAT) for modeling molecules and materials with rotational symmetry.

super_nodes.label: Crystal graph neural network architectures
super_nodes.gloss: Nearly all members are graph neural network architectures for crystals and molecules (CGCNN, Graph Attention and Transformer Networks, Graph Convolutional Networks, materials graph networks).

super_nodes.label: Melting temperature prediction and phase transitions
super_nodes.gloss: Centers on predicting melting temperatures and phase transitions with ML (gradient-boosted trees, symbolic regression, phase-field simulations) using features like cohesive energy and elastic moduli.

super_nodes.label: Classical ML regression and clustering methods
super_nodes.gloss: Centers on classical ML regression and clustering tools (SVR, Kernel Ridge Regression, k-means, Random Forests, SHAP) and cluster-expansion methods applied to materials property prediction.

super_nodes.label: Materials Project and open databases
super_nodes.gloss: Nearly all members describe the Materials Project database, API, and ecosystem and related open materials-data infrastructure (Open Catalyst, ColabFit, Materials Data Facility) and their applications.

super_nodes.label: DFT software and benchmark datasets
super_nodes.gloss: A mix of DFT and electronic-structure software (Quantum ESPRESSO, CP2K, OpenMX, deal.II) and materials or molecular benchmark datasets (OMat24, OC20, OQMD, WBM, QM9).

super_nodes.label: Evaluation metrics for benchmarking models
super_nodes.gloss: Centers on evaluation metrics and scoring methods (Silhouette, Calinski-Harabasz, ROC-AUC, F1, Spearman correlation) used to benchmark ML models on tasks like rMD17 and 3BPA.

super_nodes.label: JARVIS software ecosystem and tools
super_nodes.gloss: Almost entirely components of the JARVIS software ecosystem (JARVIS-DFT, JARVIS-FF, JARVIS-ML, JARVIS-Tools, heterostructure-design apps) for high-throughput materials computation.

super_nodes.label: MLIP loss functions and training techniques
super_nodes.gloss: Centers on loss functions and training techniques for MLIPs: Hessian-augmented training, weighted RMSE losses, and Voigt-Reuss-Hill or O(3) averaging schemes for energy and force predictions.

super_nodes.label: DFT computation methods and convergence
super_nodes.gloss: Centers on DFT computational methods and their convergence and optimization (DFT+U variants, D4FT direct minimization, k-point and electronic convergence criteria, automated failure detection).

super_nodes.label: ML prediction of DFT Hamiltonians
super_nodes.gloss: Centers on the universal HamGNN model and related architecture (Wigner-Eckart layer, LCMP layer) for predicting DFT Hamiltonian matrices with machine learning.

super_nodes.label: Optimization methods for structure relaxation
super_nodes.gloss: Centers on optimizers (Adam, AdamW, BFGS, conjugate gradients) and structural-relaxation techniques, including MLIP-accelerated pre-relaxation pipelines (M3GNet, MACE-MP-0, CHGNet) compared with DFT.

super_nodes.label: Convex hull stability and geometry
super_nodes.gloss: Centers on convex-hull stability analysis and geometric descriptors (PCA, UMAP, neighbor-list matrices) used to assess local atomic geometry and thermodynamic stability.

super_nodes.label: Materials ML benchmarking tools and pipelines
super_nodes.gloss: Centers on Automatminer and related materials-ML benchmarking software (Matbench, Matminer, MatPES, LLM-agent frameworks like MatPilot and LLMatDesign) for automated property prediction.

super_nodes.label: Benchmarking universal MLIP model performance
super_nodes.gloss: Centers on benchmarking universal MLIP models (PET, MatPES-trained models, TransIP, NequIP) on accuracy and speed across matbench-discovery, MADBench, and MD-17 tasks.

super_nodes.label: Force prediction and energy conservation
super_nodes.gloss: Centers on force prediction in MLIPs, especially conservative versus non-conservative force models, energy-conserving architectures (SchNet, GAP, ACE), and training strategies for force accuracy.

super_nodes.label: Phonon prediction with ML models
super_nodes.gloss: Nearly all members concern predicting phonon spectra and dispersion with ML/GNN models (Phonax, VGNN, PET-OAM) benchmarked against DFPT reference data.

super_nodes.label: Classical and ML interatomic potentials
super_nodes.gloss: Centers on classical interatomic potentials (Lennard-Jones, Finnis-Sinclair, MEAM, Born-Meyer) and early ML potentials (Behler-Parrinello, Deep Potential, GAP) plus related DFT approximations (r2SCAN, GW).

super_nodes.label: Monte Carlo sampling methods
super_nodes.gloss: Centers on Monte Carlo sampling techniques (Metropolis, kinetic MC, umbrella sampling, Billiard Walk) and adaptive Maxwell-Boltzmann priors for generating training or simulation data.

super_nodes.label: Author citation references
super_nodes.gloss: Entirely a list of author-name citations (Qi et al., Batzner et al., Batatia et al., and others); no shared topic beyond being paper references.

super_nodes.label: MD-17 molecular benchmark datasets
super_nodes.gloss: Mostly the MD-17 and CCSD(T) small-molecule benchmark datasets (aspirin, benzene, ethanol, etc.), plus a few unrelated tools (SOAP, FireWorks, Swish activation).

super_nodes.label: GNN message-passing architecture components
super_nodes.gloss: Centers on architectural components of graph neural networks for message passing (embedding layers, interaction blocks, edge/vertex updates, virtual or global nodes), as in AlphaFold-style networks.

super_nodes.label: GNN model benchmark performance results
super_nodes.gloss: Centers on benchmark accuracy results for GNN and MLIP models (CGCNN, CHGNet, SchNet, MPNN, DeePMD-kit) on standard datasets like QM9, MD17, ISO17, and Matbench Discovery.

super_nodes.label: Atomic descriptor basis representations
super_nodes.gloss: Centers on basis-set representations and descriptors for atomic environments (Coulomb matrix, Gaussian and spherical-harmonic radial bases, Bessel and Fourier expansions) used in GNN inputs.

super_nodes.label: Gaussian quadrature and cutoff functions
super_nodes.gloss: Centers on Gaussian quadrature accuracy for phase-space and energy integration and cutoff-function design (smooth, adaptive, envelope functions) to avoid discontinuities in potential-energy surfaces.

super_nodes.label: Ewald summation and long-range corrections
super_nodes.gloss: Centers on Ewald summation variants (particle mesh, reciprocal-space, Latent Ewald Summation) and related long-range and dispersion correction methods (Harris-Foulkes, Blochl, vdW corrections) in DFT.

super_nodes.label: Model fitting and analysis modules
super_nodes.gloss: A mix of model components for potential fitting (GAP-style fitting network, hypernetwork, filter-generating network) and analysis modules (MSD, Arrhenius, free-energy fitting); fairly heterogeneous.

super_nodes.label: Train-test splitting and OOD evaluation
super_nodes.gloss: Centers on train/test splitting strategies (cross-validation, OOD-composition and OOD-element splits, maximal separation) and benchmark sets (WBM, CSP Blind Test) for evaluating model generalization.

super_nodes.label: Diverse MLIP methods and applications
super_nodes.gloss: A diverse mix: activation functions (softplus, S2 activation), LLM-based materials-design agents (LLMatDesign, MatPilot), autonomous synthesis (A-Lab), and ionic-conductor activation-energy predictions; no single tight theme.

super_nodes.label: ML model efficiency and scalability
super_nodes.gloss: Centers on computational efficiency and scalability of ML models (Mixture of Experts, model compression, CUDA and precision tradeoffs) and challenges of AI-driven multiscale modeling.

super_nodes.label: Atomistic simulation tools and embeddings
super_nodes.gloss: Centers on atomistic simulation software (ASE, atomate, Embedded Atom Method) and atom-level embedding and energy-decomposition schemes used across various ML potentials.

super_nodes.label: Magnetic moments and long-range charges
super_nodes.gloss: Centers on incorporating magnetic moments and long-range electrostatics into MLIPs (CHGNet magnetic-moment charge proxy, Latent Ewald Summation, CELLI, DPLR) for accuracy and charge transferability.

super_nodes.label: Voronoi methods and matrix decomposition
super_nodes.gloss: A mix of Voronoi tessellation methods (features, decomposition, CUR reconstruction), QR-based reparameterization for D4FT, and a couple of formate-on-copper studies; fairly diverse.

super_nodes.label: Lithium-ion diffusion and conductivity prediction
super_nodes.gloss: Nearly all members concern predicting lithium-ion diffusivity, conductivity, and migration barriers with MLIPs (LiFlow, CHGNet, TensorNet-MatPES, MACE-MP-0) compared against AIMD and experiment.

super_nodes.label: Neural network normalization and attention
super_nodes.gloss: Centers on neural-network regularization and attention mechanisms (layer normalization, dropout, multi-head and self-attention, RBF attention biases) used to stabilize and improve equivariant model training.

super_nodes.label: DeepH models and magnetic skyrmions
super_nodes.gloss: Centers on DeepH and xDeepH models predicting DFT Hamiltonians for 2D and magnetic materials (CrI3, MoS2, graphene, skyrmion supercells), reproducing band structures with high accuracy.

super_nodes.label: ML training workflows and strategies
super_nodes.gloss: Centers on training strategies and workflows for ML models: active learning, multi-task and multi-modal training pipelines, iterative and two-stage (BF16/FP32) training schedules.

super_nodes.label: MAE evaluation metrics and formulas
super_nodes.gloss: Mostly MAE-based evaluation metrics (energy, force, formation-energy MAE) for benchmarking models, plus a few superconducting-Tc formulas (McMillan, Allen-Dynes) and melting-temperature clustering results.

super_nodes.label: MLIP pretraining and fine-tuning strategies
super_nodes.gloss: Centers on pretraining and fine-tuning strategies for MLIPs (OMat24, GNoME, eSEN, TransIP) and their extension to predicting vibrational spectra and free energies (Phonax).

super_nodes.label: Catalysis and adsorption energy prediction
super_nodes.gloss: Centers on predicting adsorption energies for catalytic systems (AdsorbML, EquiformerV2, UMA-M on OC20) and related validation, oxidation-state, and stoichiometry methods.

super_nodes.label: Symmetry-adapted features and descriptors
super_nodes.gloss: Centers on symmetry functions and symmetry-adapted or invariant descriptors (order parameters, parity indices, SO(3) irreps, Reynolds-operator polynomial features) used to encode structure symmetry.

super_nodes.label: ML models matching DFT accuracy
super_nodes.gloss: Nearly all claims show ML or DFT-approximation models (GAP for silicon, HamGNN, D4FT, SevenNet-0) reproducing DFT-level accuracy for energies, band gaps, elastic constants, and defects.

super_nodes.label: Workflow automation and data infrastructure
super_nodes.gloss: Centers on workflow-automation infrastructure for materials science (AFLOW, FireWorks, MatPES generation, REST-APIs) and emerging autonomous or AI-agent workflows (Human-in-the-Loop, Chain-of-Thought reasoning) for experimentation.

super_nodes.label: ConvLSTM fracture prediction in crystals
super_nodes.gloss: Entirely about using a ConvLSTM model to predict crack paths and fracture toughness in crystalline materials, generalizing from single-crystal to bicrystal data.

super_nodes.label: Atomic descriptors for MLIP models
super_nodes.gloss: Centers on atomic-environment descriptors used in MLIPs (DeepPot-SE, SOAP, CFID, free-volume descriptors) and comparisons of their accuracy for property and percolation prediction.

super_nodes.label: Uncertainty quantification in ML models
super_nodes.gloss: Centers on uncertainty quantification and confidence estimation for ML models (ensemble model deviation, Bayesian estimation, latent-space distance, confidence heads) tied to trustworthiness and robustness.
